title: Allow for delaying rejecting play() promise for blocked plays until metadata loaded
body:
The specification for HTMLMediaElement.play() includes the following clause to allow playback to be blocked:

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#playing-the-media-resource:media-element-28

>     If the media element is not allowed to play, return a promise rejected with a "NotAllowedError" DOMException\.


But consider the case where we immediately call play() upon creating a video element:
```
let v = document.createElement("video");
v.src = "resource.mp4";
let p = v.play();
```

In Firefox we want the ability to block play() calls for resources with audio tracks which are not muted and volume>0, and we won't know until we've reached readyState>=HAVE_METADATA whether a resource has audio tracks.

We also don't want to unilaterally block all play() calls before we have loaded metadata, as the resource may not have an audio track, and therefore can't be audible, and we want that to be able to autoplay.

So we don't have enough information at the time play() is called in the case above as to whether we should reject the play() promise at step 1 of the play() function specification.

The spec seems to only allow us to reject the play() promise for blocked autoplay as the first step. We'd like to reject it later, once we've loaded the resource's metadata. It would be nice if we could do so without violating the spec. :)

Also when we do reject the play() promise further into the load, we need it specified what other events should also be fired, i.e. we should fire a "pause" event if the value of the paused flag is false when we decide to reject the pending play promise (i.e. if we fired a "play" event at step 6.3 of the play() function spec).
